sentences.text:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Navneet Kumar For the Petitioner : Mr. Din Dayal Saha ,
Advocate For the State : Mr. Sunil Kumar Dubey, Advocate 04/15.02.2024
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the State.

2. The instant Criminal Revision is directed against the order taking cognizance dated 19.11.2016 passed by the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Rajmahal in connection with Rajmahal P.S. Case No. 138 of 2016 dated 21.09.2016 corresponding to G.R. No. 491 of 2016 whereby and where under, the learned court below, has taken the cognizance against the opposite party no.2 Hashim Sk.

Under Section 498A and 504 of the IPC, however did not take cognizance against opposite party no.3 Ikiramul Sk., opposite party no. 4 Sarjahatan Bibi and one Enamul Sk.
3.

It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the gist of the allegations as set out in the FIR is that initially a case was lodged on 13.07.2016 by way of Complaint Case No. 672 of 2010 which was later on converted into FIR on 21.09.2016 being Rajmahal P.S. Case No. 138 of 2016, registered for the offence under Section 376, 498A, 307 and 506 of the IPC against 4 accused persons including the opposite party no.2,3 and 4 and one Enamul Sk.

It has been contended on behalf of the petitioner that the opposite party no.2 had committed rape with the petitioner, who was a married woman on 17.09.2015 and thereafter, a panchayati was convened, where the earlier husband of the petitioner, divorced her, and thereafter the petitioner solemnized the marriage with the OP No. 2,
Hashim Sheikh and thereafter she went to her matrimonial house.

Further it has been alleged by the petitioner that when she went to her matrimonial home after solemnizing the marriage with the OP No. 2, she was subjected to harassment and cruelty for want of fulfilment of demand of dowry and she was assaulted and ousted from her matrimonial house and thereafter this case was instituted.

4. It has further been submitted that the police, after the investigation, submitted the final report exonerating all the co- accused persons from the all the charges except the O.P. No.2, against whom the charge-sheet was submitted for the offence punishable under section 498-A and 504 of the IPC Kausara Bibi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109934849/
1 and he was exonerated from the offence punishable under section 376 of the IPC as no evidence has been found by the police during the course of the investigation for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.

sentences.text:
It has been submitted that the Learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Rajmahal while taking the cognizance after accepting the final form, has committed gross error because there were ample evidences in the case diary against all the accused persons including the O.P. No.2, 3 and 4 for the offence punishable under Section 376, 498-A 506 of the IPC but the learned court below not only exonerated the opposite party no. 3 and 4 from all the offences and cognizance has been taken only against O.P. No.2 and that too only against 498 A and 504 of the IPC and therefore a gross error has been committed.
5.

On the other hand, the learned A.P.P., appearing on behalf of the state, submitted that the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Rajmahal has rightly taken the cognizance on the basis of the evidences in the case diary because the charge-sheet was submitted only against O.P. No.2 for the offence punishable under section 498 A and 504 of the IPC, since, there was no evidence under Section 376, therefore no cognizance has been taken against him for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC.

Further, it has been pointed out that there was no evidence of any kind of offence either under Section 376 or 498 A or 504 of the IPC against the co-accused person i.e., O.P.
No.3- Ikramul Sk., O.P No.4- Sarjahatan Bibi, and therefore, final report was submitted showing lack of evidence against them and therefore, they were exonerated from the said offences and as such, it is submitted that there is no illegality in the impugned order and this Criminal Rivision Application is fit to be dismissed, being devoid of merit.
6. Having heard the party, perused the record of the case.
7. It is an admitted case of the prosecution that the petitioner has solemnized marriage with opposite party no.2, as per Muslim rights and rituals.

Further, it is found that on earlier occasion, a complaint case vide Complaint Case No. 672 of 2016 was instituted against 4 accused persons including Opposite Party no.2 Hasim Sk., opposite party no.3 Ikramul Sk., opposite party no.4 Sarjahatan Bibi and one Enamul Sk., which was later on forwarded to the concerned police station which was registered as Rajmahal P.S. Case No. 138 of 2016 dated 21.09.2016 under section 376,
498-A,307 and 506 of the IPC.

The Police, after investigation, exonerated the co-accused persons for the offences attributed in the FIR and only the husband, opposite party no.2 was sent up for trial for the offence punishable under section 498 A and 504 of the I.P.C.
8.

From the case diary, it appears that none of the independent witnesses has supported the case of the prosecution for the offence punishable under section 376 or 307 IPC against the opposite party no.2, rather, independent witnesses namely Md. Naimuddin, who has been examined on behalf of the prosecution at para 9 of the case diary; Naushad Ali at para 8 of the case diary; Ziddi Sheikh at para 10 of the case diary; Nijamuddin Sheikh at para 11 of the case diary and Zamiruddin Sheikh at para 12 of the case diary have totally falsified the case of the prosecution as they have consistently and uniformly stated in their statements recorded by the police during the course of the investigation under section 161 Cr.P.C that the petitioner has falsely instituted the case for the offence punishable 376 and 307 of the IPC, against all the accused persons and only the husband-opposite party no.2, is liable and that too for the case of torture and cruelty for want of Kausara Bibi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109934849/
2 non-fulfillment of dowry but no offence under section 376 or 307 of the IPC has been supported by these persons and thus, it is manifest that the investigating officer has rightly appreciated the statements of the independent witnesses recorded during course of investigation and came to the conclusion that it is the husband opposite party no.2, who is the only culprit for the offence punishable under Section 498-A and 504 of the IPC and no offence against opposite party no.3 and 4 has been found at all and further no offence of either under Section 376 or 307 of the IPC has been substantiated against O.P. No.2 except for the offence punishable under Section 498A and 504 of IPC.
9.

sentences.text: From the impugned order it also appears that the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st class, Rajmahal has rightly appreciated the contents of the case diary and the statement of the witnesses recorded and took cognizance only against the opposite party no.2 for the offence punishable under Section 498 A and 504 of the IPC.

10. In view of the aforesaid discussion made in the forgoing paragraphs, this Court does not find any illegality in the impugned order dated 19.11.2016 passed by the Judicial Magistrate 1st Class,
Rajmahal.
Accordingly, the instant Criminal Revision is dismissed being devoid of merits.

(Navneet Kumar, J.) A.Mohanty Kausara Bibi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109934849/
